source.title: Understanding Language Model Scaling on Protein Fitness Prediction
source.authors: Chao Hou; Di Liu; Aziz Zafar; Yu-Feng Shen

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary figure captions are present. Some equation text is garbled, but the reported findings relevant to this record are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates scaling in protein language models and finds that mutation-effect prediction can decline as perplexity falls and model size increases, refining the idea that better language-model prediction necessarily brings better downstream performance.
record.gate_note: The study measures ESM2 perplexity and mutation-effect prediction across model sizes, datasets and proteins. Figures 1, S1, S3 and S5 provide plotted results without exact values in the text; those are recorded as figure only. The paper also discusses earlier work, which is not recorded as a result here.
record.test_reason: The study measures ESM2 zero-shot mutation-effect prediction across model sizes (8M–15B) and per-protein perplexity on two datasets. It reports a rise-then-fall relation: lower perplexity and larger size do not reliably bring better downstream performance. This is a direct result against V6 in protein language models.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors add that larger pLMs overfit by memorising wild-type residues, which collapses the LLR dynamic range. They also propose excluding low-perplexity proteins during training to optimise pLMs for mutation-effect prediction.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates masked-residue ESM2 inference and zero-shot mutation-effect prediction across protein datasets and model sizes; it does not fit the original text-model scaling laws or their compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Mutation-effect performance depends on per-protein perplexity, the number of homologs, and protein category; low-perplexity declines are particularly reported for larger models and proteins with sufficient homologs.
record.problems: The relevant scaling and performance results are mainly shown in figures, with exact values not stated in the text. The reported downstream task is protein mutation-effect prediction rather than a range of language-model downstream tasks; some analyses use representative proteins or per-protein plots.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately quantified model-by-model values are stated in the text for the plotted series. Figure 2's medium-sized-model examples are not assigned a specific checkpoint in the text, so they are not entered as a separate model row.

untested.parts: No fit of pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No variation of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Perplexity is reported to fall with ESM2 size, but no power-law form is fitted for protein models.
Text language models, downstream tasks other than zero-shot mutation-effect prediction, and fine-tuned or few-shot downstream use.
No fitting choices or exponents examined.

missing.what: Median perplexity falls consistently with ESM2 model size on both datasets (all sizes), with no fit of the curve's form.
missing.locator: Figure 1B–C; main text 'larger ESM2 models consistently achieve lower perplexity'
missing.versions: V5 (cannot_determine power-law form); context for V6

missing.what: Performance of the smaller ESM2 models (8M, 35M, 150M) against 650M in the model-size series. Without it, r1 and r4 have no baseline.
Small models show no low-perplexity decline. The decline appears mainly in larger models and for proteins with many homologs; proteins with few homologs never reach low perplexity.

record.verdict_notes: Every result is figure-only; the text gives no exact correlations. The four proteins in Figure 2 were chosen for showing the rise-then-fall trend. The study is a short preprint without peer review. The domain is protein masked language models, not text models. The ESM2-15B results used float16 inference.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit held-out pretraining loss power laws against parameters, tokens or compute, or test bottleneck conditions.
Does not fit scaling laws on small runs or test predictions on substantially larger runs.
Does not compare parameter and token allocations at fixed compute or fit compute-optimal allocation trends.
Does not vary depth, width or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Uses protein language models, but does not test whether pretraining-loss power laws hold in protein models or other training regimes.
Tests mutation-effect prediction with ESM2, not a broad set of downstream tasks or downstream performance as a function of fitted text-pretraining loss laws.
Does not fit loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits, or systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule or fitting method.

relationships.condition: ESM2 models larger than 650M, and proteins with perplexity below 3–6
relationships.reason: ESM2-3B and ESM2-15B underperform ESM2-650M on both datasets despite lower perplexity. Per-protein performance falls as perplexity drops further, through lost context understanding (r2, r3, r5, r6, r9, r11, r15).
relationships.display_finding: ESM2-3B and ESM2-15B underperformed ESM2-650M on both datasets, and further perplexity reductions below 3–6 coincided with worse per-protein performance and lost context understanding.

relationships.condition: Peak location, substitution specificity at low perplexity, and viral/designed proteins
relationships.reason: Performance peaks at perplexity 3–6 (r8). Substitution specificity shows no significant change at low perplexity (r13). Viral and designed proteins score lower at comparable perplexity, so loss alone does not predict performance (r16).
relationships.display_finding: Performance peaked at perplexity 3–6, substitution specificity showed no significant change at low perplexity, and viral or designed proteins scored lower at comparable perplexity.
